glosses: To sell at a reduced price.

examples.text: Sales were slow even after the shop discounted the product.

glosses: To deduct from an account, debt, charge, etc.

examples.text: Merchants sometimes discount five or six per cent for prompt payment of bills.

glosses: To disregard an account or regard as unimportant.

examples.text: Owing to his reputation, they discounted his comments.
Of the three opinions, (I discount Brown's), under this head, one supposes that the law of Causality is a positive affirmation, and a primary fact of thought, incapable of all further analysis.

glosses: To lend money upon, deducting the discount or allowance for interest.

examples.text: The banks discount notes and bills of exchange.

glosses: To take into consideration beforehand; to anticipate and form conclusions concerning (an event).

examples.text: The market has dropped, discounting changes in interest rates.

glosses: To believe, or act as though one believes, that one's own feelings are more important than the reality of a situation.

examples.text: For the summer sale, there was 40% discount in all the stores at the mall.
This store offers discounts on all its wares. That store specializes in discount wares, too.

glosses: A deduction made for interest, in advancing money upon, or purchasing, a bill or note not due; payment in advance of interest upon money.
The rate of interest charged in discounting.

examples.text: On our approaching the house where the Misses Spenlow lived, I was at such a discount in respect of my personal looks and presence of mind, that Traddles proposed a gentle stimulant in the form of a glass of ale.

glosses: The act of one who believes, or act as though they believe, that their own feelings are more important than the reality of a situation.
Specializing in selling goods at reduced prices.

examples.text: If you're looking for cheap clothes, there's a discount clothier around the corner.
